rows.answer:
The search results don't include any Demo Bank rule on gold collateral, so this answer comes from the RBI Directions alone.

The main rule is that the lower of two prices is used. Gold or silver accepted as collateral is valued at the reference price for its actual purity, and the lower of the 30-day average closing price and the previous day's closing price is used, as published by the India Bull
rows.expected_answer: Lower of 30-day average closing price or previous day's closing price for that purity

This comes from paragraph 11 of the RBI Commercial Banks (Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025
rows.expected_answer: Not less than one day; set by the bank's credit policy
